content.comment_body: Hello everyone, My [product_name] [article_no] is connected to a LAN via a router. I want to perform remote software downloads over the internet and also exchange data, similar to what I can do locally on the LAN. Could someone specify which TCP/IP ports are used by [product_name] so I can set up access through a NAT (Network Address Translation) router? Thank you all for your assistance, wishing you a great day.

You can change the IP address of [product_name] in the network menu, but only when it is in STOP mode, not RUN mode. Assign a local LAN address (for example: 192.168.1.10), a netmask of 255.255.255.0, and set the gateway to your router's address (for example: 192.168.1.1). If you want to access [product_name] from outside your LAN, forward TCP port 10001 to its IP address. You will then connect using the external IP address of your LAN (which you can find using websites like whatismyip.com). The router will forward your connection to [product_name]. If your network uses DHCP without a static external IP, you might also need a dynamic DNS service.
[product_name] [article_no] operates on TCP/IP port 10001. Thanks again, [user_name]. It works!

analysis.insight_summary: A user requested details on TCP/IP port settings needed for remote access to a [product_name] device through a NAT router, for both software downloads and data exchange over the internet. The discussion clarified specific port forwarding requirements and addressed network configuration steps, enabling successful remote connectivity. This highlights the value of straightforward networking guidance in documentation or user interfaces.
